turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hi, thanks for coming in today. What's been going on for you lately?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Not much. Work let me go a few weeks ago. It's fine though, gives me more time to sort out the thing with my neighbors. They've been making a bit of a racket, you know?

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Yes, I understand that can be stressful. Is there anything else going on that you'd like to talk about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It's just...sometimes the people next door talk about me through the wall. I don't know, maybe it's just the apartment, but it feels like they're in here with me sometimes.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That must be difficult. Is there anything else that might be helpful for us to talk about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I don't know...I just feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to happen, you know? It's hard to explain. (pauses) I've been trying to stay busy, but it's not the same as having a job.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That's understandable. Anything else you'd like to talk about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (sighs) I don't know...just feeling a bit...restless, I suppose. Like I'm not really doing anything with my time, even when I am trying to stay busy. (pauses, looks away)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Is there anything else you'd like to talk about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (shrugs) No, I think that's it. I just need to get some things sorted out, that's all.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Alright. Is there anything else I can do to help?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looks down, fidgets with hands) No, I think I'm okay for now. Just...just need some time, I guess. (pauses, then stands up)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Alright. I'm here if you need anything.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (nods, starts to walk out, then stops and turns back) It's just...the people next door. They're always watching. (looks at you with a hint of unease)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Is there anything else I can do to help?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looks away, voice barely above a whisper) Just leave the door open a bit, okay? When I'm in my apartment, I mean. It makes me feel...safer.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Of course. I'm here if you need anything.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (nods, turns to leave, but then pauses) And...can I ask you something? Do you ever feel like...people are watching you too? Even when you're alone? (looks at you with a mixture of curiosity and wariness)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Yes, I have felt that way sometimes. But it's okay. We can talk about it if you want.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (takes a step back, eyes narrowing slightly) No, it's not okay. Not for me, anyway. I mean...I know it sounds crazy. But it's just...I know what I feel. (pauses, looks away)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Is there anything else I can do to help?
